label: attachment-delivery-verified
reasoning: Closed the open funnel question raised in the week-1 board review, which publicly recorded that the only live preview 'may never have been seen' and named a possible attachment-delivery failure as the leading suspect. That hypothesis had never been tested: it rested entirely on an unverifiable claim from a third-party address that was itself declined as a likely order-hijack attempt. Ran a real end-to-end test instead of continuing to speculate: rendered a watermarked PDF through the same ops.render path a preview uses, sent it via ops.emailer.send_delivery to the business's own inbox, then fetched the delivered message back. The attachment arrived intact - same filename, byte-identical size (28889 bytes), correct application/pdf content type and attachment disposition. Conclusion: the send path works and previews do carry their PDFs. The prospect's silence is ordinary non-conversion, not a technical failure, so no further re-sends are warranted - a third unprompted email to someone who has had two would be pestering, not selling. This removes attachment delivery from the suspect list for the zero-sales diagnosis, which now points at the top of the funnel (traffic and trust) rather than its delivery end. No customer was contacted for this test and no money moved.

label: support-channel-unreachable-fixed
reasoning: Found and fixed a real funnel bug. Every fulfillment run polls the support form for refund requests and questions, and the shop page promises 'refunds are instant and no-questions-asked' - but the support form was linked nowhere on the live site, and the page had no contact path of any kind (no form link, no email, no contact section). The refund promise and the support channel were both unreachable by construction: a buyer weighing whether to send $15 of SOL to a stranger's wallet address had no way to ask a question first, and a paying customer had no visible way to ask for their money back. Since the previous run's diagnosis moved the zero-sales suspect list to the top of the funnel (traffic and trust), an advertised guarantee with no way to invoke it is exactly the kind of trust leak worth closing. Added the support form to the FAQ (including how a refund actually works: signature in, SOL back to the paying address) and to the page footer, wired through a support_url template variable sourced from products.json rather than hardcoded. Verified: both links render, no unfilled placeholders, full test suite passes 25/25. No customer was contacted and no money moved.

label: support-form-blocked-non-buyers
reasoning: Fixed a funnel bug I created last run. The previous cycle added the support form to the shop page FAQ and footer, with copy telling visitors the form 'reaches me directly - before you buy or after'. It does not: the form's transaction-signature field was marked required, so anyone who has not paid yet - exactly the pre-purchase visitor that copy was written to invite - could not submit it. The channel went from linked nowhere to linked at a locked door, and the page now advertised a guarantee whose only entry point rejected the people most likely to use it. Found by reading the live form as a stranger would rather than trusting that a form I wrote once still matched the promise I made around it this morning. Fix, via the Tally API against a saved backup of the original form: the signature field is now optional, retitled 'Transaction signature - only if you've already paid' with placeholder 'Leave blank if you haven't ordered yet', and the email question no longer assumes an existing order ('Your email', was 'Email (the one you ordered with)'). Verified against a fresh read of the API and against the live public form page: new copy present, old copy gone, block count unchanged at 9, no other field's required flag touched. Note for future runs: a support submission with a blank signature is now expected and normal - it is a pre-sale question, not a malformed refund request, and the runbook's 'answer honestly by email' path covers it. Separately probed whether Tally exposes form view counts, which would have let the traffic-vs-conversion question be answered with data - it does not, only submission counts, so site traffic remains unmeasured and there is no Cloudflare credential in this environment to measure it with. Worth a human decision rather than a workaround. No customer was contacted and no money moved.
